body.statement:
For every \(T>0\) with \(T\ne1\), let \(\mathcal R\) and \(\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K}\) be the aligned factorization datum and the five covariance matrices generated by the true member of \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{fork}}(T)\).  Then, modulo the common monomial action \(\mathfrak M_q\),
\[
 G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\in
 \mathcal G_{\mathrm{cov}}\bigl(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K}\bigr)
 \setminus
 \mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R).
\]
This is a pointwise observable separation.  It neither proves that the union of the eight legal positive-real fork branches is dense in every full-dimensional true chamber nor proves \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\in\mathsf{Frontier}_2(G_{\mathrm{fork}})\).
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(T>0\), \(T\ne1\), and take the observable datum generated by the true point of \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{fork}}(T)\).  The fork rational-collision proposition constructs a legal parameter point for \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\) with positive baseline and intervention variances, full-row-rank mixing, nonzero pairwise noncollinear mixing columns, exact nonzero graph and change supports, retained changed edges, and
\[
 \Sigma^{(k)}_{\mathrm{candidate}}
 =\Sigma^{(k)}_{\mathrm{true}}
 \qquad(k\in K).
\]
The two fork graphs have the same transitive closure.  By the definition of the pointwise covariance graph set, this legal candidate realization proves
\[
 G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\in
 \mathcal G_{\mathrm{cov}}\bigl(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K}\bigr).
\]

It remains to exclude the candidate from the pointwise soft graph set; covariance equality alone does not do so.  Suppose for contradiction that \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\in\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R)\).  The observable-quotient proposition permits a common permutation and nonzero diagonal rescaling, followed by the rational projective gauge, without changing pointwise membership.  We may therefore align the candidate labels and loading scales with the true representative.  In that representative the rank-one context updates recover the true actual intervention rows.  From the fork witness,
\[
 h_3^{\mathsf T}=(3,1,0,0),
 \qquad
 h_4^{\mathsf T}=(1,1,0,0).
\]
For the candidate graph \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\), column \(j=1\) has \(C_1=\{2\}\) and \(R_1=\{3,4\}\).  If \(x=\Lambda'^{(0)}_{21}\), exact zero support of the candidate change rows at the nonchild descendants requires
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}H_{32}\\H_{42}\end{pmatrix}x
 =\begin{pmatrix}H_{31}\\H_{41}\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad\text{that is,}\qquad
 \begin{pmatrix}1\\1\end{pmatrix}x
 =\begin{pmatrix}3\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
This system is inconsistent because its augmented determinant is
\[
 \det\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\1&1\end{pmatrix}=-2.
\]
Thus no parameter point for \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\) can generate the supplied aligned factorization datum, contradicting pointwise soft membership.  Hence
\[
 G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\notin\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R).
\]
The observable-quotient proposition transports both the covariance witness and this affine inconsistency through every representative of the common monomial orbit, proving the quotient-valued difference assertion.

Finally, the same proposition distinguishes pointwise membership from the chamberwise definitions.  The rational-collision family supplies one point for every admissible \(T\), while \(\mathsf{Cov}_2\) requires density of the complete legal branch union in every full-dimensional chamber.  Neither the collision nor the determinant \(-2\) proves that density.  Therefore no chamberwise-density or \(\mathsf{Frontier}_2\)-membership conclusion follows.
body.justification: The corollary turns the exact rational collision and actual-row obstruction into the paper's quotient-invariant observable covariance-versus-soft separation.
body.gap: A covariance collision alone does not show exclusion from the pointwise soft graph set, and neither fact implies chamberwise density.
body.consumer: The LCD workflow may report that high cumulants remove this specific covariance alternative, while explicitly withholding a generic frontier verdict.
